# Benchmark results (generated by `python -m eval.run_eval` — do not edit by hand)

Synthetic KESTREL-3U dataset, seed 2026, 42 questions, retrieval depth k=10 for the baselines.

| Metric | graph_agent | vector_only | fulltext_only |
|---|---|---|---|
| Answerable: macro F1 | 1.0 | 0.142 | 0.152 |
| Answerable: exact set match | 1.0 | 0.027 | 0.054 |
| Answerable: macro precision | 1.0 | 0.182 | 0.181 |
| Answerable: macro recall | 1.0 | 0.179 | 0.195 |
| Out-of-scope: correct abstention | 1.0 | 0.0 | 0.0 |
| Median latency (ms) | 0.41 | 0.57 | 1.11 |

F1 by category:

| Category | graph_agent | vector_only | fulltext_only |
|---|---|---|---|
| coverage | 1.0 | 0.137 | 0.143 |
| decision | 1.0 | 0.0 | 0.0 |
| impact | 1.0 | 0.189 | 0.192 |
| out_of_scope | 1.0 | 0.0 | 0.0 |
| risk | 1.0 | 0.111 | 0.0 |
| structure | 1.0 | 0.0 | 0.083 |
| supplier | 1.0 | 0.833 | 1.0 |
| trace | 1.0 | 0.0 | 0.095 |

Limitations: the questions and the agent's keyword rules were written by the same author, so the
graph agent's score is an upper bound for this question set. Baselines are told the answer node type.
The embedding is a lexical hashed trigram vector, not a neural model.
